description:
Ballindooley Castle is a five-storey tower house of the late 15th century, about 6 km north of Galway city on the N84. It is believed to have been built around 1480 by the de Burgo (Burke) family, and Ballindooley Lough lies to the south-west.

The first recorded owner is Redmond Regough Burke, and the tower probably served as a “guest castle” for the Burkes, one of the Tribes of Galway. According to local accounts, the British gunboat Helga bombarded it during the 1916 Rising because rebels were believed to be gathering there to march on Galway. The tower was then left abandoned for about two centuries, until a Chicago lawyer bought it in ruins around 1990 and restored it over more than twenty years, adding a new slate roof and a stone parapet and repairing the machicolations. In March 2022 the owner, Barry Haughian, took in four Ukrainian families at the castle.

The castle is rented whole as a self-catering stay, not room by room. It offers about 3,400 sq ft, including a main hall on the third floor and a murder hole above the entrance, on half an acre of lawn with gated access. There is no restaurant or staff on site, and it is not open to day visitors: only guests renting the whole castle can enter.

Galway city is about 15 minutes away, with Connemara and the Aran Islands further west.

faqs.answer: No. It is private, and only guests renting the whole castle can enter; there are no day visits.

faqs.question: What happened at Ballindooley Castle in 1916?

faqs.question: How far is Ballindooley Castle from Galway city?

**On-site:** Self-catering only — no restaurant, bar, or staff on-site during the stay.
